content: The test image shows a soybean plant with mostly green leaves, but with notable yellowing in the lower/middle canopy. Stems appear to remain green. No obvious leaf spots or lesions. This pattern of lower leaf yellowing with green upper canopy on what appears to be a relatively healthy-looking plant warrants checking Sudden_death_syndrome and Green_stem_disorder.

The Green_stem_disorder reference shows mature/dying plants with only stems remaining green — very different from the test image. The test image shows an actively growing plant with green leaves and some lower leaf yellowing.

**Analysis:**
- Test image: Soybean plant with mostly green canopy, yellowing concentrated in lower/middle leaves
- Stems remain green throughout
- No distinct leaf spots, lesions, or pustules visible
- Growing in dry/sandy-looking soil
- Upper canopy looks relatively healthy

This pattern of lower leaf yellowing while upper canopy stays green is characteristic of **Sudden_death_syndrome** (SDS), which causes interveinal chlorosis/necrosis starting from lower leaves, with root rot symptoms that cause foliar symptoms to progress from bottom up. The overall plant structure with yellowing at the base also fits Phytophthora, but SDS is more commonly associated with this gradual lower-to-upper yellowing pattern on otherwise green-stemmed plants.
